source.title: Reliability of analog resistive switching memory for neuromorphic computing

confidence_rationale: Authoritative reliability review documenting that analog RRAM persistent state is NOT a clean latch: cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability, conductance drift/relaxation, retention loss, finite endurance, random telegraph noise, and ~4-6-bit effective precision. Weakens the 'scales without losing stability' clause. Low mapping_fidelity (measured on memory crossbars, not REE).
failure_signatures: Conductance drift and C2C/D2D variability mean a value written as a hard boundary will have moved by read-time; effective precision caps at ~4-6 bits; random telegraph noise injects ongoing stochastic read fluctuation.

Mitigations (write-verify, closed-loop programming, redundancy) are statistical, never a hard guarantee -- so a deterministic externally-checkable threshold cannot be assumed without continuous re-verification overhead.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A major bottleneck for analog resistive switching memory in neuromorphic computing is reliability -- endurance and retention degradation, read/write noise, conductance drift, C2C/D2D variability and RTN -- intrinsic to stochastic set/reset filament physics and only mitigable, not eliminable.
mapping.ree_translation: Speaks to Q-066's STABILITY axis: the substrate's 'persistent state' drifts and fluctuates stochastically, so any hard threshold encoded in conductance is a moving target -- removing the assumption that persistent state means stable, auditable state.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Drift/variability measured on memory crossbars for DNN inference, not on any REE substrate; that these media drift does not by itself prove REE's specific stability/safety invariants break.
mapping.source_context: Device-reliability review of analog RRAM for neuromorphic computing.

confidence_components.notes: Real device-physics measurements mapped to REE's abstract stability requirement.
